feedback: No reviewer point was proven by a failing reproduction, so none blocks; they are listed above as open notes.
unproven: The ArchitectureDiagram component adds two SVGs (wide and stacked) always, causing duplicate diagram content and violating the requirement that on phones a second stacked variant should be hidden via CSS without duplication for screen readers. The current implementation renders both SVGs with class "arch-stacked" always, not conditionally hidden, and both have accessible <title> and <desc> (mounted true after hydration) potentially causing duplicate content for screen readers. The task requires the stacked variant to be hidden via CSS (display:none) and not be aria-hidden, and only one set of <title>/<desc> needed. Adjust ArchitectureDiagram to render a single SVG for desktop and conditionally hide the stacked one with CSS (e.g., using media queries and `aria-hidden` appropriately).

EngagementsPage renders Enterprise tier card as <article id="enterprise">, but the test expects a generic element with id "enterprise" (not necessarily article) and specifically checks that the enterprise card is wrapped in <article>. However the test suite's weak_tests indicate that this expectation is questionable. The test currently fails because it expects the enterprise card to be an <article> element, but the task only requires an element with id "enterprise" (any tag). The implementation uses <article>, which may cause failure in tests expecting a different element type. Align the markup to the test expectation by using a generic <section> or <div> with id "enterprise" instead of <article>.

EngagementsPage includes a "Not sure which fits?" line inside a <section class="not-sure"> but the test expects it to be placed below the tiers and not inside an article element. The current structure may not match test ordering expectations; adjust the placement to ensure the line appears after the tier cards and before any other container, and ensure it doesn't contain an article tag.
